items.originalTitle: Why fertile male killifish outlive their peers
items.title: Why fertile male killifish outlive their peers
items.summary: Why do some individuals of the same species live significantly longer than others? In evolutionary biology and aging research, this question is often linked to a trade-off between reproduction and survival. The underlying idea is that energy and resources invested in reproduction may lead to compromises in repair and maintenance, thereby hindering a long life. Thus, the assumption is that particularly successful reproduction at a young age comes at the cost of a shorter lifespan.

items.originalTitle: The faintest supernova ever observed refuses to go out, staying visible for nearly a year
items.title: The faintest supernova ever observed refuses to go out, staying visible for nearly a year
items.summary: An international team of astronomers, including Paul Groot of Radboud University, has discovered that a supernova explosion does not always have to be extremely bright. The team has identified the faintest supernova observed to date. It remained visible for an exceptionally long time and appears to have been caused by a so-called white dwarf and a relatively small companion star. The discovery may have implications for our understanding of the evolution of binary stars and the measurement of the expansion of the universe. The results were published in Nature Astronomy.

items.originalTitle: ‘Genuinely emotional’: the world-conquering Chicken Shop Date’s final, eye-opening episode
items.author: Stuart Heritage
items.title: ‘Genuinely emotional’: the world-conquering Chicken Shop Date’s final, eye-opening episode
items.summary: After a 12-year run, Amelia Dimoldenberg’s last episode of Chicken Shop Date – a therapy session with Esther Perel – is being shown in cinemas. It’s a fittingly grand finale for a YouTube cult favourite that far outgrew its medium The decision to screen the full final series of Chicken Shop Date in cinemas before the finale airs on YouTube is, it could be argued, overkill. The cinema is a place where you sit rapt among like-minded people, bombarded with cutting-edge sound design and world-class visuals. On the other hand, the fun interview show that is Chicken Shop Date is the thing I watch alone on my computer while I pick my toenails. It isn’t a natural fit, is what I’m trying to say. And yet, goddamn it if the whole thing didn’t leave me slightly choked up. After 12 years of flirting and awkwardness, Amelia Dimoldenberg’s final guest is Esther Perel, the Belgian psychotherapist and relationship guru beloved by Oprah Winfrey. It is by no means a traditional episode, almost completely dismissing the tone of everything that came before it. Dimoldenberg’s well-honed persona, alternately dismissive and needy, is nowhere to be seen. Instead, Dimoldenberg does something that Perel must be deadeningly familiar with when meeting new people: she uses the episode as a free therapy session.

items.title: New Yorkers and Tourists Try to Salvage a Parade Day Postponed by Rain
items.summary: Wind and rain grounded the beloved balloons that typically dominate the Thanksgiving skies, leaving the streets along the parade route mostly deserted on Thursday.
